explanation: Benzene reacts with concentrated nitric acid (with sulfuric acid as catalyst) via electrophilic aromatic substitution to form nitrobenzene and water.

beaker_view.initial_appearance: Colourless benzene mixed with concentrated nitric and sulfuric acid, usually cooled in an ice bath.
beaker_view.final_appearance: A pale yellow, oily liquid (nitrobenzene) that separates as its own layer, denser than water.
beaker_view.observation: The colourless benzene layer turns into a pale yellow, oily liquid with a faint almond-like smell, settling out as a distinct layer once the mixture is left to stand.
